verdictRationale: hx-text-input is a well-implemented form-associated component with strong ARIA patterns. No critical or high violations found. The single medium finding (cross-shadow aria-labelledby for slotted labels) is a known browser-compatibility concern documented in the project's own accessibility guidelines. All core WCAG 2.1 AA criteria for text inputs are met. The three low findings are enhancement opportunities rather than violations.

passChecks.title: ElementInternals correctly implements form association
passChecks.description: The component correctly uses static formAssociated = true and attachInternals() (via HelixElement base). setFormValue() is called on every value change. setValidity() is called with all three arguments (flags object, message, anchor element — the native input) enabling browser-native validation UI. All form lifecycle callbacks are implemented: formResetCallback resets value and interaction state, formStateRestoreCallback restores string state, formDisabledCallback propagates disabled to the property.

passChecks.title: aria-invalid correctly set on native input during error state
passChecks.description: aria-invalid='true' is set as a string value (not a boolean attribute) on the native <input> when either the `error` property is set or the error slot has slotted content. The check uses `hasError = !!this.error || this._hasErrorSlot`, ensuring both sources activate the error state. aria-invalid is correctly omitted (using the Lit `nothing` sentinel) in non-error states to avoid aria-invalid='false' being present, which is correct per ARIA spec.

passChecks.title: role=alert and aria-atomic on error container
passChecks.description: The error message container correctly uses role='alert' and aria-atomic='true'. There is no redundant aria-live attribute present (a prior P1-01 issue that was resolved). The role='alert' pattern provides assertive announcement of error messages to screen readers when they appear dynamically. The error div is only rendered when hasError is true, so the role='alert' is not present in the DOM in non-error states, which prevents phantom announcements.

passChecks.title: aria-describedby correctly wires error and help-text IDs
passChecks.description: The aria-describedby computation on the native input correctly references the error div ID when hasError is true, and the help-text div ID when helpText property is set or help-text slot is filled. Both IDs are within the same shadow root as the native input, avoiding cross-shadow-boundary resolution issues. When both error and help-text are present (slotted help-text case), both IDs are space-separated in aria-describedby, which causes screen readers to announce both descriptions.

passChecks.title: Label association via for/id within same shadow root
passChecks.description: When the `label` property is set, a <label> element is rendered inside the shadow root with `for` pointing to the native input's deterministic ID. Both the label and the input are within the same shadow root, so the for/id association is valid. IDs are generated using a module-level counter (createIdCounter) rather than Math.random(), making them SSR-safe and hydration-stable.

passChecks.title: Focus ring visible for all focus interactions
passChecks.description: Focus styling is applied via :host([focused]) .field__input-wrapper and :host([focused-visible]) .field__input-wrapper in CSS, driven by FocusMixin's focused/focusedVisible reflected attributes. The .field__input-wrapper:focus-within rule also provides a CSS-native fallback. The focus ring uses design tokens (--hx-focus-ring-color, --hx-focus-ring-width) with hardcoded fallbacks (#60a5fa, 2px). The focus ring is always visible when the input has focus, satisfying WCAG 2.4.7 minimum requirements.

passChecks.title: Keyboard navigation follows native input behavior
passChecks.description: All keyboard interaction is handled by the native <input> element, which provides complete browser-native keyboard support for text, email, password, tel, url, search, number, and date types. Tab/Shift-Tab moves focus in and out. FocusMixin correctly delegates focus() and blur() to the native input. The autofocus attribute is respected via firstUpdated() in FocusMixin.

passChecks.title: Required field indicator is accessible
passChecks.description: The visual required asterisk (*) is wrapped in <span class='field__required-marker' aria-hidden='true'>, correctly hiding it from screen readers. The native `required` attribute on the input provides the semantic required state for AT (maps to aria-required via HTML-AAM without needing an explicit aria-required attribute). No redundant aria-required is set, following the 'prefer native semantics' principle.

passChecks.title: autocomplete attribute support
passChecks.description: The `autocomplete` property is passed through to the native input, allowing consumers to set any valid HTML autocomplete token (name, email, username, current-password, etc.). This satisfies WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose) for inputs that collect personal data. The component does not restrict or override autocomplete values.

passChecks.title: aria-label passthrough for unlabeled usage
passChecks.description: The ariaLabel property (attribute: aria-label) is forwarded to the native input via aria-label=... Consumers can provide an accessible name when a visible label is not used (e.g., a search input in a toolbar). This satisfies SC 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value for inputs that intentionally omit visible labels.

passChecks.title: prefers-reduced-motion respected
passChecks.description: The @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in the styles file sets transition: none on .field__input-wrapper, disabling the border-color and box-shadow transitions that animate the focus ring. This respects users who have indicated they prefer reduced motion, satisfying the healthcare project's motion accessibility requirement.

passChecks.title: Disabled state correctly communicated
passChecks.description: The native `disabled` attribute is passed to the <input> element, which browsers automatically communicate to assistive technology. The `disabled` attribute also reflects to the host element (:host([disabled])) allowing CSS targeting. formDisabledCallback propagates fieldset-level disabled state to the component property, ensuring correct behavior within disabled fieldsets.

passChecks.title: Focus delegation to native input
passChecks.description: FocusMixin overrides focus() and blur() on the host element to delegate to the native input via the _focusableNode getter. This ensures that programmatic focus (e.g., el.focus()) reaches the native input rather than the custom element host, which is important for AT that calls focus() programmatically.

passChecks.title: axe-core violations: zero in all four tested states
passChecks.description: The test suite includes axe-core audits (via the project's checkA11y utility) for four component states: default (with label), error state, disabled state, and required state. All four pass with zero violations as documented in AUDIT.md (2026-03-11 deep audit) and confirmed by the test file's Accessibility section.

findings.title: Slotted label aria-labelledby crosses shadow DOM boundary
findings.description: When a label element is provided via the 'label' slot (the Drupal Form API pattern), the component assigns an ID to the slotted element in the light DOM (slottedLabel.id = `${this._inputId}-slotted-label`) and then sets aria-labelledby on the native <input> inside the shadow DOM to reference that light DOM ID. Per the ARIA specification and this project's own accessibility-workflow.md guidelines, aria-labelledby ID resolution does not cross shadow DOM boundaries. Chromium resolves this via its composed tree accessibility implementation, but Firefox (Gecko) and older Safari do not guarantee cross-shadow ID resolution. This means the slotted label may not be correctly associated with the input in non-Chromium browsers, leaving the input effectively unlabeled for screen readers in those environments.
findings.fix: For the slotted label case, use internals.ariaLabelledBy (ARIA element reflection via IDL) or internals.ariaLabel as fallback. Alternatively, extract the text content of the slotted label and pass it as aria-label on the native input when _hasLabelSlot is true and ariaLabel is not explicitly set. The project's accessibility-workflow.md explicitly states: 'aria-labelledby cannot cross shadow boundaries — use aria-label or internals.ariaLabel instead.'

findings.title: focused and focused-visible CSS rules are visually identical — no keyboard-differentiated focus ring
findings.description: FocusMixin provides both `focused` and `focused-visible` reflected attributes to distinguish pointer-initiated focus (focused=true, focusedVisible=false) from keyboard-initiated focus (both true). The CSS in hx-text-input.styles.ts applies the same visual focus ring style to both :host([focused]) and :host([focused-visible]). This means there is no visual distinction between mouse-click focus and keyboard Tab focus. While WCAG 2.4.7 only requires a visible focus indicator (not differentiation by modality), the emerging WCAG 2.4.11 and 2.4.12 criteria encourage enhanced keyboard focus visibility. The focusedVisible infrastructure exists but is unused — it represents an accessibility enhancement opportunity that would benefit keyboard users.
findings.fix: Consider styling :host([focused]:not([focused-visible])) .field__input-wrapper with a subtler focus indicator (e.g., no box-shadow, only border-color change), and reserving the full focus ring (border-color + box-shadow) for :host([focused-visible]) .field__input-wrapper. This provides the optimal experience: pointer users see a lighter focus state, keyboard users see the full high-contrast ring. Note: WCAG 2.4.7 AA compliance is maintained either way — this is an enhancement.

findings.title: touched interaction state advances only on value change, not on focus-blur
findings.description: In FormMixin, _handleInteractionBlur() is the hook that advances the `touched` state to true. In hx-text-input, this hook is called from _handleChange(), which fires on the native `change` event. The native `change` event fires only when the input loses focus AND the value has changed. If a user focuses the input and then tabs away without typing anything, `touched` remains false, and `pristine` remains true. This means validation UX patterns that rely on `touched` (e.g., 'show required error only after the user has interacted with this field') will not trigger for blur-without-change interactions. While not a direct WCAG violation, this can lead to validation errors appearing only after form submission rather than inline as the user fills the form, which is a WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) best practice.
findings.fix: Add a @blur event listener on the native input that calls this._handleInteractionBlur() independently of the change event. This is the standard approach: 'touched' should become true whenever the field has received AND lost focus, regardless of value change. Example: add `@blur=${this._handleBlur}` to the input element and implement `private _handleBlur(): void { this._handleInteractionBlur(); }` in the component class.

findings.title: color-mix() for focus ring opacity has limited browser support
findings.description: The focus ring box-shadow calculation uses color-mix(in srgb, <color> calc(var(--hx-focus-ring-opacity, 0.25) * 100%), transparent) to create a semi-transparent focus ring. color-mix() requires Chrome 111+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.2+. In browsers without support, the box-shadow will render as the full-opacity focus color rather than the intended semi-transparent variant. This is graceful degradation (the focus ring IS visible, just slightly different in appearance) so it does not violate WCAG 2.4.7. However, in environments with strict browser version requirements (such as enterprise healthcare environments using older browsers), the focus ring may appear more visually prominent than intended by the design.
findings.fix: This is an acceptable low-severity item and matches the existing AUDIT.md documentation. If older browser support is required, consider providing a fallback box-shadow without color-mix: box-shadow: 0 0 0 var(--hx-focus-ring-width, 2px) var(--hx-input-focus-ring-color, ...) with a custom property for opacity control, or use a CSS @supports block to conditionally apply color-mix.
